36932-romney.title: Romney
36932-romney.creator: Unknown
36932-romney.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. High over the western boundary of Cavendish Square rose a tripod wooden scaffolding, supporting a gigantic crane cutting the arch of the sky; on windy days the smoke from the engine was blown upwards into space. Below, twentieth-century mansions were growing on the site of old Harcourt House, for Cavendish Square, like the rest of London, was suffering an architectural change into something strange and new.

40759-the-old-road.title: The Old Road
40759-the-old-road.creator: H. Belloc
40759-the-old-road.description: A book by H. Belloc. There are primal things which move us. Fire has the character of a free companion that has travelled with us from the first exile; only to see a fire, whether he need it or no, comforts every man. Again, to hear two voices outside at night after a silence, even in crowded cities, transforms the mind.

arxiv-2106-05475.title: Jointly Optimize Coding and Node Selection for Distributed Computing over Wireless Edge Networks Cong T. Nguyen, Diep N. Nguyen, Dinh Thai Hoang, and Eryk Dutkiewicz are with University of Technology Sydney, Australia (email: cong.nguyen@student.uts.edu.au, Hoang.Dinh, Diep.Nguyen, and Eryk.Dutkiewi
arxiv-2106-05475.creator: Cong T. Nguyen, Diep N. Nguyen, Dinh Thai Hoang, Hoang-Anh Pham and Eryk Dutkiewicz
arxiv-2106-05475.description: Abstract This work aims to jointly optimize the coding and node selection to minimize the processing time for distributed computing tasks over wireless edge networks. Since the joint optimization problem formulation is NP-hard and nonlinear, we leverage the discrete characteristic of its decision variables to transform the problem into an equivalent linear formulation.

arxiv-2301-06479.title: Combinatorial Hopf species and algebras from preorder cuts
arxiv-2301-06479.creator: Gunnar Fløystad
arxiv-2301-06479.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Gunnar Fløystad. We introduce new concepts and viewpoints on combinatorial Hopf species and algebras. We give a category 𝐬𝐞𝐭 ℕ {\rm\bf set_{{\mathbb{N}}}} whose objects are sets, and (dualizable) morphisms represented by matrices of non-negative integers. For a bimonoid species ( B , Δ , μ ) (B,\Delta,\mu) in 𝐬𝐞𝐭 ℕ {\rm\bf set_{{\mathbb{N}}}} we may then dualize the product μ \mu to get two intertwined coproducts Δ , Δ ′ \Delta,\Delta^{\prime} .

arxiv-2406-08617.title: Satellite Drag Analysis During the May 2024 Gannon Geomagnetic Storm
arxiv-2406-08617.creator: William E. Parker and Richard Linares
arxiv-2406-08617.description: Abstract Between May 10-12, 2024, Earth saw its largest geomagnetic storm in over 20 years. Since the last major storm in 2003, the population of satellites in low Earth orbit has surged following the commercialization of space services and the ongoing establishment of proliferated LEO constellations.

arxiv-2508-17962.title: “Nobody should control the end user”: Exploring Privacy Perspectives of Indian Internet Users in Light of DPDPA Conference: ; ; CCS: Security and privacy Usability in security and privacy
arxiv-2508-17962.creator: Sana Athar, Devashish Gosain, Anja Feldmann, Mannat Kaur, Ha Dao
arxiv-2508-17962.description: Abstract . With the rapid increase in online interactions, concerns over data privacy and transparency of data processing practices have become more pronounced. While regulations like the GDPR have driven the widespread adoption of cookie banners in the EU, India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA) promises similar changes domestically, aiming to introduce a framework for data protection.

arxiv-2601-08252.title: Resumming Scattering Amplitudes for Waveforms
arxiv-2601-08252.creator: and Andrea Cristofoli
arxiv-2601-08252.description: Abstract We develop a formalism to compute non-perturbative 5-point scattering amplitudes and apply it to gravitational waveforms in the two-body problem for arbitrary trajectories. Drawing inspiration from Feshbach’s projector formalism in nuclear physics, we introduce effective potentials governing graviton emission and relate them to perturbative scattering amplitudes at arbitrary order in the gravitational coupling and mass ratio.

arxiv-2602-17552.title: TopoSZp: Lightweight Topology-Aware Error-controlled Compression for Scientific Data Corresponding author: Sheng Di, Mathematics and Computer Science Division, Argonne National Laboratory, 9700 Cass Avenue, Lemont, IL 60439, USA
arxiv-2602-17552.creator: Tripti Agarwal 1 , Sheng Di 2 , Xin Liang 3 , Zhaoyuan Su 4 , Yuxiao Li 5 , Ganesh Gopalakrishnan 1 , Hanqi Guo 5 , Franck Cappello 2
arxiv-2602-17552.description: Abstract Error-bounded lossy compression is essential for managing the massive data volumes produced by large-scale HPC simulations. While state-of-the-art compressors such as SZ and ZFP provide strong numerical error guarantees, they often fail to preserve topological structures (e.g., minima, maxima, and saddle points) that are critical for scientific analysis. Existing topology-aware compressors address this limitation but incur substantial computational overhead.

pmc-10571371.title: “Publish or Perish”: barriers to research publication in an undergraduate medical research program
pmc-10571371.creator: Abdulrahman F Alsulami, Zeyad O Khaimi, Mohammed A Hadi, Yazeed H Aljabri, Talha S Mayet, Alaa Althubaiti
pmc-10571371.description: ObjectivesPublication is one of the crucial parameters in research, and the inability to publish has been noted in many medical students’ projects due to different reasons. This cross-sectional study aimed to determine the obstacles that prevented medical students in a health science university from publishing their research from 2018 to 2021.

pmc-11522961.creator: Alba Gómez-Valadés, Rafael Martínez-Tomás, Sara García-Herranz, Atle Bjørnerud, Mariano Rincón
pmc-11522961.description: Machine learning (ML) methodologies for detecting Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) are progressively gaining prevalence to manage the vast volume of processed information. pmc-13185418.title: Influence of ocular biometry on peripheral retinal visualization: a comparative study of Clarus and Optos widefield imaging systems
pmc-13185418.creator: Christoph Spartalis, Andreea Fisus, Manuel Ruiss, Oliver Findl
pmc-13185418.description: BackgroundThe purpose was to compare the Clarus 500 and Optos Daytona widefield imaging systems with respect to the farthest clinically assessable peripheral retinal structure in each quadrant, and to evaluate whether ocular biometry, particularly axial length and spherical equivalent, influences device specific widefield performance.

pmc-13293665.creator: Alexander Siegel, Jennifer Gamache, Kyaw Min Tun, Wuttiporn Manatsathit
pmc-13293665.description: Strongyloidiasis is a parasitic infection endemic to warm and moist climates, which is caused by the intestinal nematode Strongyloides stercoralis. In the United States, most cases are seen in immunocompromised patients residing in the Northeast and East South-Central regions and in travelers from endemic regions.

pmc-13528143.creator: Antonia Geupel, Patricia Gaillard, Rainer Haak, Heide Glaesmer
pmc-13528143.description: BackgroundDentistry involves substantial physical, psychological, and organizational demands. Increasing administrative tasks and structural changes in dental health care may exacerbate imbalances between professional effort and rewards. According to the Effort-Reward Imbalance (ERI) model, such imbalances are linked to adverse mental health outcomes.
